milestone: M44 External Mode Pack Registry Update Selection

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds Rust-owned registry manifest selection for the currently active external Mode Pack before candidate fetch/provenance/update admission.
Requires explicit caller authorization, expected manifest hash, and current activation fingerprint before selecting a bounded update candidate.
Persists bounded registry selection evidence without raw registry, candidate, provenance, signature, key, or ledger payloads.
Gives scheduled callers a deterministic next candidate and provenance URL set for the existing verified update pipeline.

answers.strategic_capabilities: mode_pack_runtime with runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: A headless caller can authorize a bounded HTTPS registry manifest read, verify the exact manifest hash, match the active remote Mode Pack, and receive one bounded update candidate/provenance selection.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing candidate fetch requires the caller to already know one candidate URL and cannot select from a registry using current active Mode Pack evidence.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: External Mode Pack updates remain manual URL handoffs, preventing a safe registry-driven update loop for long-running autonomous development.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M39-M43 because it selects an update candidate before fetch/provenance/trust/admission; it does not rewrap those later checks.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. A new runtime action is required because no existing RPC accepts a registry manifest URL plus expected manifest hash and current activation fingerprint to produce a bounded candidate selection.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase returns only bounded selection evidence needed to drive existing fetch/provenance/admission calls, not a report/history/digest/readiness/inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime now rejects stale, mismatched, duplicated, unsafe, unbounded, or unhashed registry selections and persists one replay-safe selection event.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can deterministically move from current active external Mode Pack state to the exact next candidate/provenance fetch inputs.
answers.milestone_progress: Completes the first M44 vertical slice by turning external Mode Pack registries into a runtime-owned update candidate selection step.

exit_criteria: modepack.selectRegistryUpdate requires explicit registry selection authorization
registry URL is validated as bounded HTTPS with no credentials, fragments, local/private hosts, redirects, or unsupported ports
registry manifest response is byte bounded, UTF-8 JSON, sensitive-scan checked, and verified against expected_registry_manifest_sha256
selection requires expected_current_activation_fingerprint to match the active remote_https_candidate Mode Pack
manifest must contain exactly one matching entry for active Mode Pack name and source_kind
selected candidate/provenance URLs and all fingerprints are validated and returned as bounded evidence
selection is persisted and replayed without duplicate ledger events
RPC and ledger results do not include raw registry manifest, candidate content, provenance statement, signatures, public keys, raw ledger payloads, prompts, stdout/stderr, or environment

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M44.1 adds runtime-owned external registry selection; review must confirm it is a bounded execution capability and not a report surface.
